references.text: The regulation concerning the sin offering with a male goat for a leader who has sinned, showing the background for this offering.
Aaron was commanded to take a male goat as a sin offering, the same type of offering that the tribal leaders brought.
On the Day of Atonement, two male goats were taken as sin offerings, illustrating the male goat as the usual animal for sin offerings.
The first time the sin offering with a male goat is mentioned is in the consecration offering from the leader of the tribe of Judah.
A male goat as a sin offering for the entire congregation when they sin unintentionally.
A male goat as a sin offering at the New Moon festival, the same type of offering as at the dedication of the tabernacle.
King Hezekiah's use of male goats as sin offerings for the kingdom, showing that this practice continued.
At the temple dedication after the exile, male goats were used as sin offerings for all Israel.
The book of Hebrews contrasts the blood of goats and bulls with Christ's blood, which completely cleanses from sin.
